rv.q: The low-key approach mutes Munro’s humour and makes a long play seem longer, even as it renders a fractured relationship compelling and sad.
The sheer quality of the acting ensures a visit to Iron is worthwhile.
This is a riveting production that takes hold, keeping the audience with bated breath until the very last moment.
It’s a remarkable and brilliant piece of writing.

cn.t: Munro's probing prison drama about a mother-daughter reunion after 15 years earns praise for its exploration of justice and family bonds, with real-life mother-daughter casting of the Mackies adding authentic resonance to this slippery, thought-provoking work.
